title: The Years Before the Ring
style: Adult contemporary, conversational New Englander female vocals in the first verse, wide range climbing into top notes with crooning legato phrasing as the chorus melody opens; piano-led chords, brushed drums and warm bass; quick, restless fills in a restrained midtempo pulse; close vocal, spare accompaniment, sparse harmony voices spaced in roomy reverb.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You held the phone beside his bed
and said, “Steve, it’s Aurora.”
You tilted it until he saw me.
I’d forgotten how you say his name.

The week we brought him home,
we moved his chair beside the window.
You asked him where he wanted it.
He pointed a little to the left.

[Chorus]
Thank you, Maureen,
for the years before the ring,
for the ten since you got married,
for the life you made with him.
I used to think the story
was in how it all began.
Nearly twenty years together.
I’m beginning to understand.

[Verse 2]
You called from work to ask about his lunch.
I told him it was you.
He waited till I’d finished, then he said,
“Ask her if she’s had hers too.”

You came home with your work shoes on
and told him who’d been in that day.
He knew which names would make you laugh.
I heard you from the kitchen.

[Bridge]
I used to count from the wedding.
There was a date I could put down.
Now I think of all those evenings
when I was living out of town.
I’d send a text. He’d send one back.
You knew how his day had gone.

[Final Chorus]
Thank you, Maureen,
for the years before the ring,
for the ten since you got married,
for the life you made with him.
Nearly twenty years together.
I can take tonight.
Go tell Dad about your day.
I’ll bring the plates in when they’re ready.
